title: RISE equity fund changes and 2026 gas rates
subtitle: Also covers a new public artwork for Upper Canada Park and a strategic plan update item.
overview: The Finance and Corporate Services Committee recommended changes to the RISE grant, which funds community groups led by and serving Black, Indigenous and other racialized residents. The changes focus on newer groups, narrow the funding categories, move to one intake a year and require funded work to be delivered in Kitchener {{vote:m2}}.

The committee also recommended new 2026 natural gas delivery rates for Kitchener Utilities customers, effective January 1, 2026 {{vote:m3}}. Staff said the average residential customer would pay about $3.33 more per month. Staff plan to draw on a stabilization reserve and extra winter revenue to soften the increase.

On the consent agenda, the committee recommended approving a new public artwork, "The Seams," for Upper Canada Park {{vote:m1}}. A strategic plan update was on the agenda as an information item, with no vote recorded. These are recommendations, and Council will make the final decisions.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council endorse revisions to the RISE funding framework so it better matches the evolving needs of equity-denied communities.
The committee recommended approving Kitchener Utilities' natural gas variable and fixed delivery rates for all delivery customers, effective January 1, 2026.
The committee recommended commissioning the artwork "The Seams" for Upper Canada Park and authorizing the Mayor and Clerk to sign an agreement with the artist team.

debate: On RISE, one councillor asked how to make applications easier. Staff said applicants find the form easy but struggle with grant-writing terminology. They plan a single guide, info sessions and workshops, and are talking with regional funders about a shared application.

Councillors asked how much RISE money was spent on events outside Kitchener. Staff said the data was not collected, since location was not asked in the pilot and the contracts did not require it. Staff offered to look into it and will make the location requirement clear in future agreements.

Staff explained that prioritizing groups operating five years or less is meant to level the field. Established groups have more grant-writing capacity, but they can still apply and have other funding options.
Staff said they would welcome Council direction to review broadening RISE to other equity-denied groups in 2027. They noted that this would increase applications and the investment needed.

On gas rates, a councillor asked about avoiding a larger increase. Staff said drawing more on the stabilization reserve would only push the problem into future years. They also pointed to the multi-year cost of aging gas infrastructure and uncertainty over how the energy transition will affect gas use.
